quest.title: They Who Abandoned the Past
quest.description: Jahoda has received a new commission from the Adventurers' Guild. However, for Jahoda, this commission seems a little different than usual...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3, Ragged Doll x1

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, looks like you handled the commission without a hitch. Thank you, Miss Jahoda. Here is your payment.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: See? Told you it'd be fine! Not a bad payout either, hehe... Got any more quick-Mora jobs like that?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I can certainly take a look. One moment please...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Eh!? Isn't that...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hey, Katheryne... Was that pendant over there used for posting a bounty?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: It was indeed — you certainly have a sharp eye, Miss Jahoda. Mr. Ihanti left it as collateral for a bounty request.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll take that one. Just give me the deets.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The only thing is... the reward for that one isn't all that high, and nowadays, pieces like this are not worth much either. I'm not sure it's the kind of job you're after, Miss Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: No worries, I'll take it. Let's call it... a bit of charity work on the side. Gotta build up some good karma once in a while, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Haha... Very well then. Please wait a moment.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: I mean, it's not like I've got much else to do right now. Can't just sit around playing with Ashru all day, can I? Nef— I mean Boss Nef'd boot me out in no time.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: #Hmm, now that you're here... {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you two are pretty handy. Wanna join forces on this one? We could split the reward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #A commission, huh? You'd better ask {M#him}{F#her} — {M#he's}{F#she's} the expert, after all!

choices.text: Seriously Paimon, you're making me blush...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Bet you it's nothing major. Trust me, Ihanti's way too much of a scaredy-cat for it to be about anything serious...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Miss Jahoda, here are the details of Mr. Ihanti's commission.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Alrighty, let's see what that little wimp's gone and—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's up? Please don't say it's something super difficult...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Nah, nothing like that. Just didn't expect a guy who couldn't even bring himself to hurt a fly to go posting life-or-death commissions like this...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: You? Hahaha, sure... Couldn't be more by-the-book if you tried, huh?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Relax, I'm just messing with you. It only mentions retrieving something from a bunch of crooks.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: To a crook, money is life, and life is money. That makes it a matter of life or death, am I right? Hahaha...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: C'mon, follow me. Pretty sure I can handle those punks by myself — odds are you won't even have to lift a finger.

choices.text: I'm a law-abiding person, just so you know...
Alright then, why not. What kinda commission we talking?

dialogues.text: Pfft, what a loser. Guy's so broke, he doesn't have a single thing worth taking.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yo, Kaleva.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Who goes th— Well, well, well, if it isn't Jahoda! What brings you here, pipsqueak?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Relax, no biggie. Word has it you swiped something from a man called Ihanti a few days back. That true?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Here, take some cash and cough up the goods. I'm feeling generous today, so let's call this me buying you off.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Ooh, look at you, acting all civilized. Guess that's what happens when you've got Nefer to watch your back, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Suppose I'd rather hold onto it. What are you gonna do about it?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Do me a favor, Kaleva. Can't you and your bunch of knucklehead bros try acting normal for a change?

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Oh please, don't tell me you came all this way expecting to do honest business with a thief...

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Or did you genuinely think I'd just hand it over on a silver platter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Feels like this negotiation went south before it even got started...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: My bad, Kaleva. Shouldn't have tried dealing with you the way Boss Nef does.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: A fist to the face is the only way to negotiate with morons like you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's drop these punks together.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Looking down on us, huh? C'mon boys, time to put this little squirt back in her place. Get 'em!

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, you win!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: See? If you'd just played along earlier, you wouldn't have ended up in this mess. Now, take the Mora and go find yourself a decent doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Hmph, is this your way of showing pity?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Save your breath and just take the Mora. If you'd rather chuck it in the water or hire thugs to jump me, that's your call.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: One thing's for sure, though — going hungry and getting beaten up both suck. Don't make things worse for yourself, Kaleva.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: The junk I snatched from that invalid is lying over there.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Aside from some spare change, it was just a painting and some busted doll. The Mora's long gone, but I haven't had time to toss the rest out yet.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Alright, final question. You referred to Ihanti as an "invalid" just now. What was that supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: It means exactly what it means. That weakling's in such a state now, you can barely tell he's still alive.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: When I first found him, he was lying there stiff as a board. I honestly thought he'd already... Y'know...

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: ...Anyway, figured he didn't need his bag any longer, so I snagged it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Mark out the spot where you last saw him.

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Where I last saw him? Guess it was about... here.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: #Alright. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I'd like to return this stuff to the client in person.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: *panting*...

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Who's there? I don't have any Mora, nothing at all... If you're here for my life, just... go ahead and take it...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I—I've brought your stuff back, Ihanti.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: ...Jahoda, is that you? I can hear your voice, but I can't see clearly anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: It's me, Ihanti, and I'm standing right here in front of you. Why didn't you come find me? You look... terrible.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Even a starving stray doesn't wander into a rich man's city... Not after all the beatings it's taken.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I'm not that kind of person, and Nef— I mean, Boss Nef isn't either.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: All the more reason why I couldn't come find you. If folks got wind that you're the type to lend a hand, they'd come banging on your door day after day.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: No one would be crazy enough to pull a stunt like that with the Boss.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: But you're always out there, secretly doing good, only to be stabbed in the back by the very people you helped.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hey. I've learned a lot from Boss Nef, y'know. No one's gonna get me good like that, ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: ...Ah, you just can't stop yourself from watching out for other people, can you, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...That's my business, and no one else's.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Heh... Maybe that's why the boss thinks so highly of you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Maybe it's the only reason I'm even still alive.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Hahaha—hurk *coughing*... You're right, Jahoda. You're right...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Anyway. If there's something I can do for you, Ihanti, now's the time to tell me.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Still the same as ever, huh... What if this was all just a big scam, or I was luring you into some kind of trap?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: You wouldn't do that. Not after how long we've known each other...

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: And that's enough to win your trust?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Come on, look at the state you're in. How could you possibly threaten me?

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Ha! Finally, we're getting somewhere. I guess saving a venomous snake that can barely open its mouth is pretty safe, all things considered... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Do me a favor, then — roll up the painting in that bag and slip it into my pocket. I haven't the strength to pick it up myself.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: I painted this with my wife and daughter. It's the only thing I still care about in the whole wide world.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: As far as I'm concerned, nothing else matters anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Heh, the old you would be in stitches hearing you say that.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Hah... and what happened to those things I once treasured above all else? They could save neither my wife, nor my life...

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: But maybe that's just the fate of a thief. Everything we steal always gets stolen back, and we wind up empty-handed again eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: That pendant I put up for the commission was all I had left... Hah, though I guess I can't really call it "mine."

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: That was the first piece of jewelry you ever stole. You must have told me the story a dozen times — how you even pulled it off, and the look on the rich guy's face when he found out.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Yeah. Anyway, it's yours now.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Who did it belong to?

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: A Snezhnayan called Holomov. He used to live in Nod-Krai, but he's probably run home to Snezhnaya by now. Don't tell me you're thinking of—

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I'm not a thief anymore, and I'm not about to start hanging onto stolen goods either. This pendant should go back to its rightful owner.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Haha... hahaha... You really are something else, Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: The boss was right... Someone like you could never... *cough* hack it as a thief... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: *coughing*...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Enough, stop wasting your breath. I'll head back and find you a doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Forget it. Just let me go the way I'm meant to.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: But—

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Jahoda, you know the boss's code.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: "Grant rest to those who seek it."

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: You know what I'm talking about, so leave me in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Fine.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: I'm glad it was you who came to help me, Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Sorry I don't have any treasure to give you. But if you want, you can have this doll.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Wait, but... I thought I told you to—

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I made this one myself. The ones you put together are long gone — I burned every last one of them, just like you told me.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Hah. Not too shabby, huh? Especially for someone who was already on the brink of going blind...

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Take it, Jahoda. Consider it my final gift.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I'll come back to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Go now. Farewell, Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Excellent, looks like you've completed the commission. Please bear with me while I fetch your payment.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Is everything okay, Miss Jahoda? You seem a little pale... You didn't run into any trouble, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Very well then. One moment, I'll be back with your payment right away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you really okay, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows we promised not to call a doctor, but... Ihanti really did look awful back there. Maybe we should—

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: No. I said I'd stick to the code, so that's what I'll do.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... you two know each other well?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: We used to be "colleagues."

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Coward he may be, but when it came to raking in the Mora... hehe, Ihanti was top shelf.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: While everyone else was out there pulling dumb scams and petty robberies, he played the game so well that people would end up willingly coughing up the cash.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: He had a real knack for talking people into things. Back when we were "working" together, he shared a lot of his skills with me... he was always taking me out for great meals, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you consider him a friend?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: A friend? Hah, 'course not. You'd have to be crazy to try making friends in that hellhole. At best, we... knew each other.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: The only reason he took such good care of me was to show off. Dragging a little sidekick along made him feel like a big shot, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: But he did look after me, I'll give him that. Helping him now is just me returning the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Alright... Here's your payment, Miss Jahoda. The Adventurers' Guild thanks you for your support!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: #Here's your share, {NICKNAME}. Thanks for the help back there.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Anyway, I should head back to the Curatorium. If the Boss wants something done and I'm not there, she'll be on my case again for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (I did say I wouldn't get him a doctor, but what's the harm in grabbing him some painkillers?)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (I'll ask the Boss to help, I'm sure she can pull some strings. Worst case scenario, I'll give up this month's pay... Actually, maybe just half of it...)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Yeah, I'll do that. I'd better get the medicine to Ihanti tomorrow...)

dialogues.speaker: Kaleva
dialogues.text: Hmph, you're a real piece of work, Jahoda, you know that? Scary smart one moment, unbelievably naive the next...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Ihanti! Ihanti! Ihaaan—

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Rest in peace, Ihanti.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: One thing's for sure — that "fate" of yours isn't gonna get me.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Not yet, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Ihanti
dialogues.text: You were right, boss... Looks like there's no escape for the wicked, after all.
